newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close at six-week low.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close at six-week low.

text.p: The Australian share market dived to its lowest closing level in six weeks on Monday on continuing concern on the future of base metal prices.
The All Ordinaries index fell 21.6 points to 2219.20.

With offshore markets regularly reaching record highs, local traders expressed dismay at the local market's lacklutre performance. "Very disappointing," said Stephen Streeter, director of institutional sales at brokerage James Capel.
"We thought it (the market) had enough in the fundamentals but it has been soft. Hills (BHP) led the market down and the golds were belted after its price fell," he said.
One broker said light turnover suggested investors preferred to stay out of the market rather than actively sell stock.
"Lots of people are waiting for the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting in the States which means we have to wait until Wednesday for the lead," said a Sydney broker.
Bellwether BHP and gold/nickel miner WMC suffered the most, their shares losing 1.37 percent and 3.31 percent respectively.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about two to one, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
